newsitem.title: USA: Muriel Siebert to develop muni unit with new hires.
newsitem.headline: Muriel Siebert to develop muni unit with new hires.

text.p: Napoleon Brandford and Suzanne Shank of the municipal bond firm Grigsby Brandford & Co have joined Muriel Siebert & Co to form a new municipal bond operation called Siebert Brandford & Shank, the securities firm said Tuesday.

"We hope to be a very important factor in the municipal bond business," Muriel Siebert, the founder of the eponymous firm, said. "I have never been as optimistic as I am now, and frankly between the three of us I think we have a reputation for being workers, hardworking people and honest people and I am very optimistic."

Brandford together with Calvin Grigsby founded the San Francisco-based municipal bond firm of Grigsby Brandford & Co, which become one of the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firms. The firm specialized in certificate of participation financings.

Grigsby resigned as chairman in September shortly after it was disclosed that federal officials were investigating bond deals the firm handled in Dade County, Fla. Grigsby has not been charged with any wrongdoing in the probe.

Brandford was named chairman of the privately-owned firm after Grigsby resigned and Shank, who had been a managing director for Grigsby Brandford in the Midwest, was named president and chief executive.
Shank Tuesday said she was unsure at this point what Grigsby Brandford's fate would be.
"We are not sure as to the status of the firm," she said.
One California municipal finance expert familiar with Grigsby Brandford's operations said the loss of Brandford and Shank could prove fatal to the San Francisco investment firm.
"It could be a mortal blow," said the expert, who asked not to be identified. He speculated that Wall Street and regional firms would try to capitalize on the shakeup.
"All that business is going to go somewhere," he said. Siebert said in addition to Brandford and Shank, "other people to be decided will join the firm."

Brandford would become chairman of the new operation, while Shank would serve as vice chairman and president. Brandford will continue to be based in San Francisco, and Shank will continue to work in Detroit and Chicago.
Thomas Mead, currently managing director of Siebert's Capital Markets Division, would become vice chair and secretary of the planned operation.
Siebert said she has met Brandford at various functions "and he always impressed me as being a very serious, solid guy."
The alliance works well from a strategic standpoint, she said.

"We know the East Coast accounts well; they are very solid on the West," Siebert said. "They are right behind the major firms in terms of originating municipal bond deals. We've been co-managers, we've been senior co-managers, but we have never led a deal. They are right in there."
